items.title: Extract the full-suite keyed scheduler into a core module shared by both callers
items.context: runScheduled and the ResourceClaim/ResourceClass types live in packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts (scheduler at :454, RESOURCE_CLASSES at :75). Move them into core without changing full-suite behaviour, so npm test and routine validate share one admission-control implementation rather than two divergent ones.
items.userSees: npm test still prints "full-suite: 47/47 passed in <N>s; retries=0; jobs=4" with no member skipped or reordered.

happy.desc: npm test still passes all 47 full-suite members with the scheduler imported from core instead of defined in the task file

edge.desc: Two schedulers running concurrently do not share cancellation state: a terminal failure in one does not mark the other run INTERRUPTED

adversarial.desc: An entry whose resource claim was never canonicalized is rejected before any process is spawned rather than scheduled with an undefined key

items.title: Declare a resource claim for every configured validate command, failing closed when undeclared
items.context: The 99-102 entries in lattice.config.json validate.commands carry only command/args/timeoutMs/focus, no resource metadata. They write under .lattice/, claim fixed ports and share the git common dir, which is why full-suite needed RESOURCE_POLICY. An undeclared command must be scheduled exclusively, never silently concurrently.
items.userSees: A validate command with no declared resource claim is scheduled exclusively and reported as such in the validate output, instead of being run concurrently by default.

happy.desc: Two validate commands with disjoint declared claims are admitted concurrently

edge.desc: A validate command with no declared resource claim is scheduled exclusively and never overlaps any other command

adversarial.desc: A claim naming an unrecognised resource class is refused at declaration time instead of being silently dropped into a shared key

items.title: Replace the sequential loop in executeValidationPlan with the shared scheduler, preserving evidence semantics
items.context: packages/main/src/core/validation-executor.ts:623 awaits each command in order. Under concurrency the following must stay identical because gates and receipts read them: commands[] entry order and content (code, durationMs, timeoutMs, optional), details[] ordering, commandExecution counts, routineValidationIdentity and identityDigest, progress/heartbeat reporting, and abortSignal/deadlineAt propagation including the deadline-exceeded throw.
items.userSees: lattice validate --story=B-xxxx --json returns the same commands[] entries in the same order with the same code and durationMs fields as a serial run, and reports the worker count it used.

happy.desc: lattice validate --json returns commands[] in plan order with the same per-entry fields (label, command, args, code, durationMs, timeoutMs) as a serial run

edge.desc: When one command fails, every remaining command still runs and commands[].length equals the plan length; the run is not cut short by scheduler cancellation

adversarial.desc: An abortSignal or exceeded deadlineAt during concurrent execution still raises the deadline error and does not report a partial run as a pass

items.title: Prove parallel equals serial on the real plan and record the measured makespan
items.context: Baseline to beat: 858s serial total measured independently in B-3434 (2026-08-16T22:58) and B-d0b8 (2026-08-17T00:09), with a 267-271s floor from quorum-submit-smoke.js and an LPT-predicted 271s at jobs>=4. The regression must assert identical per-command pass/fail sets between serial and parallel execution and no resource collision, and must surface the observed makespan so the 3.17x claim is checkable rather than asserted.
items.userSees: A smoke runs the plan both ways and prints "serial=<N>s parallel=<N>s speedup=<N>x" while asserting identical per-command outcomes; it fails if any command result differs.

happy.desc: A single regression run executes the same plan serially and in parallel and prints serial, parallel and speedup numbers measured on the same host

edge.desc: The regression fails when any command produces a different pass/fail outcome between the serial and parallel runs

adversarial.desc: The regression detects a resource collision (two conflicting commands overlapping) and fails rather than reporting a faster but unsafe run
